prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Desktop Companion", "Select a pet to bring to your desktop. Tap play to hear their voice!", "Listen to Voice"]
1: ["See Desktop Preview"]
2: ["Preparing Your Pet's Desktop Home", "Generating animations, sound effects, and desktop interaction files..."]
3: ["Select How You Want to Begin", "Pick an existing pet for instant adoption, or create a unique custom companion from photos.", "Instant Adoption vs Custom Creation"]
4: ["Signing in secures your pet data so your companion is never lost or reset."]
5: ["Photos will be rendered using your selected pet art style."]
6: ["Adoption Complete!", "Your new desktop pet is ready to keep you company. Click below to launch!", "Official Pet Owner"]
7: ["Sign In to Connect Your Pet", "Save your progress and access your pet across desktop devices."]
8: ["You can minimize the app. We'll alert you as soon as your pet is ready on your desktop."]
9: ["Meet Your New Desktop Companion", "A cute interactive pet living right on your screen to brighten your workday.", "Get Started"]
